subject: Production latency spike and priority queue blocking - Novacorp
messages:
From: Jenna Ortiz <jenna.ortiz@novacorp.com>
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.com
Cc: Novacorp SRE <sre@novacorp.com>
Date: 2027-05-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Production latency spike and intermittent 500s

Hi Aisha,

We're seeing a sudden degradation in our inference latency for the priority lane starting ~08:45 PT — p50/p90 jumped, and about 4% of requests are returning 500s. Throughput has dropped roughly 30% despite lower request volume. Our SRE team pointed at a growing queue length on the priority router and a concurrent rise in key eviction metrics for the KV cache.

I've attached a small bundle of logs (novacorp-logs-0505.zip) and a Grafana snapshot. Can your team help triage? This is impacting checkout recommendations for paying customers.

Short answer questions we need:
- Is this a config/rollout change on Redwood's side?
- Can we temporarily throttle non-priority traffic or pin to a smaller model variant?
- ETA for mitigation steps?

Thanks — this is high-priority for us.

— Jenna
Jenna Ortiz
Head of Product Operations, Novacorp

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Jenna Ortiz <jenna.ortiz@novacorp.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-05T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency spike and intermittent 500s

Hi Jenna — thanks for the heads-up and the logs. We're looking into this now. Initial ack + plan below.

What we see so far (prelim):
- Priority lane queue depth increases correlate with KV cache eviction storms in the same time window.
- There were no platform-wide config rollouts in that window on our side; a customer-specific routing tweak for another tenant coincided but doesn't map directly to your traffic.

Immediate mitigations we'll attempt (15–60m):
- Pin Novacorp's route to the current model variant and reduce autobalance to eliminate noisy neighbor influence.
- Temporarily reduce batch_size for priority lane to lower HOL blocking risk.
- Apply a conservative KV prefix TTL increase to reduce churn on hot keys.

Ask from you: please confirm whether you can accept a ~10% P50 increase temporarily if it prevents the 500s. Also, please upload any additional trace IDs if you have impacted request ids.

I've attached our runbook snapshot (runbook-priority-queue-v1.md) and asked Vivek to run diagnostic commands on the serving nodes. I'll keep you updated every 30 minutes until stable.

— Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: Jenna Ortiz <jenna.ortiz@novacorp.com>, Novacorp SRE <sre@novacorp.com>
Date: 2027-05-05T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency spike and intermittent 500s

Thanks Aisha — quick log dump and hypothesis. Attaching a snapshot (diag-snapshot-0505.png).

Observations from node diagnostics (serving zone us-west-2):
- Priority lane worker threads are spending >40% CPU on KV eviction callbacks in the 08:44–08:58 window.
- Hot key churn increased: top-100 prefixes had TTL expirations and re-populations causing synchronous prefetch storms.
- Batching stats show a rise in single-request batches for priority lane (batching bypass), while background lanes had larger batches — that mismatch increases HOL blocking on shared GPU lanes.

Hypothesis: a combination of aggressive TTL for certain KV prefixes + an imbalance in batching weights allowed background traffic to occupy batching slots, starving short-latency priority requests and causing queue growth. The KV eviction storm then forced sync reloads per prefix, amplifying latency and 500s (resource exhaustion).

Mitigation steps I can apply now (will coordinate with Aisha):
1) Increase prefix-specific TTLs for Novacorp hot prefixes to 10s from 1s (reduces churn).
2) Enforce priority-lane batch_weight floor so priority lanes are guaranteed a minimum of GPU batch slots.
3) Temporarily cap background lane concurrency for the next 45m.
4) If instability persists, fallback map for priority requests to a smaller quantized model (variant-q8) to reduce per-token compute.

I will run 1 and 2 now and share metrics within 10 minutes.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Jenna Ortiz <jenna.ortiz@novacorp.com>

Subject: Re: Production latency spike and intermittent 500s

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Please proceed with the fixes Vivek suggested.

A couple of notes from our side:
- We are willing to accept a temporary slightly higher P50 as long as p99 and error rate come down to baseline.
- Mike (cc'd) is requesting an exec-level note once there's a stable mitigation. If you can provide a 1–2 paragraph exec summary and an ETA for full root cause, that would help us close the loop.

Thanks — Jenna

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: Jenna Ortiz <jenna.ortiz@novacorp.com>, Novacorp SRE <sre@novacorp.com>
Date: 2027-05-05T13:58:00-07:00
Subject: Novacorp incident — executive summary and short-term runbook

Team — closing the immediate loop for Novacorp. Timeline and actions below for the execs and CS/SE handoff.

Executive summary (to share with Novacorp execs):
Novacorp experienced a transient production degradation caused by high churn on a small set of KV prefixes used heavily by their priority lane combined with lane scheduling imbalance. This caused short-term HOL blocking on shared GPU lanes and synchronous reloads of hot keys, producing increased p99 and a small spike in 500s. We applied configuration mitigations that stabilized error rates and reduced queue depth within ~20 minutes.

Short-term runbook (applied):
- Increased prefix TTLs for Novacorp hot keys (1s -> 10s).
- Enforced a batch_weight floor for priority lane and temporarily limited background lane concurrency.
- Pinned route to current model variant and prepared fallback to variant-q8 if needed.

Next steps (owner):
- Vivek: follow-up root-cause investigation (KV eviction policy + hot-key detection accuracy) — due EOD tomorrow.
- Rishi: coordinate a compatibility test for the quantized fallback (variant-q8) with Novacorp — due in 3 business days.
- Aisha (me): prepare the customer-facing RCA and a post-mortem deck for exec review — draft due tomorrow morning.

Attachments: diag-snapshot-0505.png, novacorp-logs-0505.zip, runbook-priority-queue-v1.md

I'll post the RCA draft to the HubSpot record (link attached) and notify Novacorp's Mike/L1 once the deck is ready.

— Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
